newsitem.title: GERMANY: Jochimsen-Buba rate rise not an issue at present.
newsitem.headline: Jochimsen-Buba rate rise not an issue at present.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen said on Monday that an increase in German interest rates was not an issue at present and said no interest rate cut was required either.
"Given the very favourable monetary conditions, demands for further rate cuts by the Bundesbank have largely fallen silent," Jochimsen said in the text of a speech.

"In addition, no one disputes the fact that there are problems in east and west (Germany), but these cannot be solved through lower rates," said Jochimsen, who is also the president of the state bank of North Rhine-Westphalia.
Jochimsen said Germany urgently needed clear and calculable fiscal policies and a speedy implementation of reforms.
"The shortcomings in these areas of economic policy cannot be covered up by monetary policy or by over-hasty entry into European monetary union," said Jochimsen.
Jochimsen also said in answer to reporters' questions: "At the moment an interest rate rise is not required."
The Bundesbank last raised German interest rates in the summer of 1992. It last cut its key discount and Lombard rates to 2.50 and 4.50 respectively in April 1996.
The central bank's main money market rate, the repo, was cut to three percent last August.
